name: Riemann Zeta Function ζ(s)
description: Computes the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) = Σ 1/nˢ (continued analytically to every real s ≠ 1).

name: Dirichlet Eta Function η(s)
description: Computes the alternating zeta function η(s) = 1 − 1/2ˢ + 1/3ˢ − … = (1 − 2^(1−s)) ζ(s).
notes: η(2) = π²/12 ≈ 0.8224670334 and η(1) = ln 2 (the formula needs the limit there).

name: Dirichlet Lambda Function λ(s)
description: Computes λ(s) = Σ over odd n of 1/nˢ = (1 − 2^(−s)) ζ(s).

name: Dirichlet Beta Function β(s) (Series)
description: Approximates the Dirichlet beta function β(s) = 1 − 1/3ˢ + 1/5ˢ − … by its first 200,001 terms.
notes: β(2) is Catalan's constant G ≈ 0.9159655942; β(1) = π/4. The error is below the first omitted term.

name: Zeta at Even Integers via Bernoulli Numbers
description: Evaluates Euler's formula ζ(2n) = (−1)^(n+1) B₂ₙ (2π)^(2n) / (2 (2n)!), with the Bernoulli number from B₂ₙ = −2n ζ(1 − 2n).
notes: n = 1 gives π²/6 (the Basel problem); n = 2 gives π⁴/90 ≈ 1.0823232337.

name: Basel Problem Partial Sum
description: Adds 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + … + 1/n², whose limit Euler found in 1734 to be π²/6.
notes: After 1000 terms the sum is about 1.6439345667, still 0.001 short of π²/6.

name: Euler Product for ζ(s) (Partial)
description: Multiplies 1/(1 − p⁻ˢ) over primes p ≤ n. As n grows it tends to ζ(s) (Euler's product formula), linking the zeta function to the primes.
notes: With primes up to 1000 and s = 2 the product is about 1.6448 against ζ(2) ≈ 1.6449.

name: Prime Zeta Function P(s)
description: Computes the prime zeta function P(s) = Σ over primes of 1/pˢ with the Möbius formula Σ μ(k)/k · ln ζ(ks).
notes: P(2) ≈ 0.4522474200: the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of all primes.

name: Apéry's Series for ζ(3)
description: Computes ζ(3) with the rapidly converging series (5/2) Σ (−1)^(k+1) / (k³ C(2k, k)) used in Apéry's irrationality proof.
notes: Each term adds about 0.6 correct digits; 20 terms give ζ(3) ≈ 1.2020569032 to full display precision.

name: Probability that k Integers Are Coprime
description: Gives the probability that k random integers have no common factor: 1/ζ(k).
notes: Two integers are coprime with probability 6/π² ≈ 0.6079; three with probability about 0.8319.

name: k-free Integers up to x
expression: sum(n, 1, x, sum(d, 1, isqrt(n), if(mod(n, d^k) == 0, mu(d), 0)))
description: Counts the integers up to x not divisible by any k-th power greater than 1, using Σ_{d^k | n} μ(d).
notes: Their density is 1/ζ(k): cube-free numbers make up about 83.2 % of all integers. There are 833 up to 1000.

name: Euler–Mascheroni Constant Estimate H(n) − ln n
description: Approximates the Euler–Mascheroni constant γ ≈ 0.5772156649 as H(n) − ln n; the error is about 1/(2n).
notes: Add 1/(2n) for a much better estimate.

name: Gauss Circle Problem: Lattice Points in a Circle
description: Counts the integer points (x, y) with x² + y² ≤ r².
notes: r = 10 gives 317 points against the area πr² ≈ 314.2; Gauss's problem is how large the difference can be.

name: Lattice Points in a Sphere
expression: sum(x, -r, r, sum(y, -r, r, if(x^2 + y^2 <= r^2, 2 * floor(sqrt(r^2 - x^2 - y^2)) + 1, 0)))
description: Counts the integer points (x, y, z) with x² + y² + z² ≤ r².
notes: r = 5 gives 515 points against the volume (4/3)πr³ ≈ 523.6.

name: Pillai's Arithmetical Function Σ gcd(k, n)
description: Adds gcd(k, n) for k from 1 to n (Pillai's function), which also equals Σ_{d|n} d φ(n/d).
notes: For n = 12 the sum is 40.

name: Sum of lcm(k, n)
description: Adds lcm(k, n) for k from 1 to n.
notes: Equals (n/2)(1 + Σ_{d|n} d φ(d)); for n = 12 the result is 468.

name: Ramanujan's Sum c_q(n)
expression: sum(d, 1, gcd(q, n), if(and(mod(q, d) == 0, mod(n, d) == 0), mu(q / d) * d, 0))
description: Computes Ramanujan's sum c_q(n): the sum of the n-th powers of the primitive q-th roots of unity, equal to Σ_{d | gcd(q, n)} μ(q/d) d.
notes: Always an integer. c_12(8) = −2, and c_q(1) = μ(q).

name: Kloosterman Sum K(a, b; m)
expression: sum(x, 1, m - 1, if(gcd(x, m) == 1, cos(2 * pi * (a * x + b * modinv(x, m)) / m), 0))
description: Computes the Kloosterman sum Σ cos(2π(ax + bx⁻¹)/m) over x coprime to m (it is always real).
notes: Weil's bound gives |K| ≤ 2√m for prime m; K(1, 1; 7) ≈ 3.4115.

name: Quadratic Gauss Sum
expression: sum(x, 0, p - 1, exp(2 * pi * 1i * x^2 / p))
description: Computes the quadratic Gauss sum Σ e^(2πi x²/p), a complex number. Gauss proved it equals √p when p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and i√p when p ≡ 3 (mod 4).
notes: For p = 7 the result is about 2.6458i = i√7. Shows complex-valued results.

name: Gamma Function Γ(x)
description: Computes the gamma function, which extends the factorial: Γ(n) = (n − 1)! for positive integers.
notes: Γ(1/2) = √π ≈ 1.7724538509. Negative non-integers work too; the poles are at 0 and the negative integers.

name: Log-Gamma ln Γ(x)
description: Computes ln |Γ(x)| without overflow, for arguments where Γ itself is astronomically large.

name: Beta Function B(a, b)
description: Computes the beta function B(a, b) = Γ(a)Γ(b)/Γ(a + b) = ∫₀¹ t^(a−1)(1 − t)^(b−1) dt.

name: Digamma Function ψ(x)
description: Computes the digamma function ψ(x) = Γ'(x)/Γ(x).
notes: ψ(1) = −γ ≈ −0.5772156649, and ψ(n + 1) = H(n) − γ for integers.

name: Euler's Reflection Formula Check
expression: gamma(x) * gamma(1 - x) - pi / sin(pi * x)
description: Checks Euler's reflection formula Γ(x)Γ(1 − x) = π / sin(πx); the difference should be 0 up to rounding.
notes: The formula underlies the analytic continuation of Γ to negative arguments.

name: Legendre Duplication Formula Check
expression: gamma(z) * gamma(z + 0.5) - 2^(1 - 2 * z) * sqrt(pi) * gamma(2 * z)
description: Checks Legendre's duplication formula Γ(z)Γ(z + ½) = 2^(1−2z) √π Γ(2z); the difference should be 0.
notes: A special case of Gauss's multiplication formula.

name: Stirling Series for ln n! (Three Terms)
description: Approximates ln n! with the Stirling series including the 1/(12n) and 1/(360n³) corrections.
notes: For n = 10 it is accurate to about 10⁻⁹: ln 10! ≈ 15.1044125731.

name: Leibniz Series for π
description: Approximates π by 4(1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/7 + …) with n terms (Madhava–Leibniz series).
notes: Converges very slowly: 1000 terms give only 3.1405926538, an error of 1/n.

name: Nilakantha Series for π
description: Approximates π with the 15th-century Nilakantha series 3 + 4/(2·3·4) − 4/(4·5·6) + 4/(6·7·8) and so on.
notes: Much faster than Leibniz: 100 terms give 3.1415924109, an error of about 2.4 × 10⁻⁷.

name: Wallis Product for π
description: Approximates π with twice the Wallis product (2·2/1·3)(4·4/3·5)(6·6/5·7)… up to n factors (1656).
notes: 1000 factors give about 3.1408077460; the error shrinks like π/(4n).

name: Machin's Formula for π
description: Evaluates John Machin's 1706 formula π = 16 arctan(1/5) − 4 arctan(1/239), which he used to compute 100 digits of π by hand.
notes: Machin-like formulas were the standard way to compute π until the 1970s.

name: Ramanujan's Series for 1/π (First Terms)
description: Approximates π with Ramanujan's 1914 series 1/π = (2√2/9801) Σ (4k)!(1103 + 26390k) / ((k!)⁴ 396^(4k)).
notes: Each term adds about 8 correct digits; one term already gives 3.14159273.

name: Chudnovsky Formula for π (First Term)
description: Evaluates the first term of the Chudnovsky series, the formula behind modern record computations of π.
notes: One term already gives 3.14159265358973, about 14 correct digits; each further term adds about 14 more.

name: Series for e (Sum of 1/k!)
notes: The error is below 1/(n · n!); 15 terms give full double precision.

name: Brun's Constant Partial Sum
description: Adds 1/p + 1/(p + 2) over twin-prime pairs with p ≤ x. The full sum converges (Brun 1919) to B₂ ≈ 1.902, even if there are infinitely many twin primes.
notes: Convergence is extremely slow: up to 10^5 the sum is only about 1.672.

name: Chebyshev Bias Count (4n+3 minus 4n+1 Primes)
description: Counts primes ≡ 3 (mod 4) minus primes ≡ 1 (mod 4) up to x. Chebyshev noticed the first group is usually ahead.
notes: The lead first changes hands at x = 26,861. Up to 10,000 the difference is 10.

name: Primes in an Arithmetic Progression
expression: sum(k, 0, (x - a) / q, isprime(a + k * q))
description: Counts the primes of the form a + kq up to x. Dirichlet's theorem says there are infinitely many when gcd(a, q) = 1, spread evenly over the φ(q) classes.
notes: Primes ending in 1 up to 10,000: 306 of the 1229 primes.

name: Siegel–Walfisz Expected Share of a Residue Class
description: Estimates how many primes up to x fall in each residue class coprime to q: π(x)/φ(q) (prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions).
notes: For q = 10 each of the endings 1, 3, 7, 9 gets about 307 of the 1229 primes below 10,000.
